paragraphs: Rabbi Nechemyah bar Mar Ukban, son of R' Yose.
He is mentioned in Jerusalem Talmud Yevamot 14:1 and quoted in Tosafot on Yevamot 113b, s.v. Yatzetah. Tosafot gives the statement as Rabbi Nechemyah’s report in the name of R’ Yehudah.

notes.text: The heading leaves the attachment of “son of Rabbi Yose” open. The printed קנג. would mean 153a, outside Yevamot’s folio range. A bounded check of Tosafot on 113a did not locate the cited comment; no corrected locator is adopted.

The saved whole Vilna TosafotYevamot113b comment beginning יצתה quotes Rabbi Nechemyah in R' Yehudah’s name from the Yerushalmi. Supplied קנג. conventionally153a remains beside113b; the earlier113a nonmatch is not erased. This match does not prove a nun/yod or amud-dot history. The heading’s son of R' Yose remains an ambiguous attachment to Nechemyah or Mar Ukban, neither relationship merged. The Yerushalmi14:1 paragraph was not newly inspected and there may refer to either work. Rabbi Nechemyah is explicit in the matched Tosafot; other abbreviated titles stay R'.

Hyman’s print (vol. III, p. 927) gives קיג. (113a), and the supplied transcription gives קנג. (153a). The named Tosafot comment is on 113b. Jerusalem Talmud Yevamot 14:1:5 names Nechemyah bar Mar Ukban and has the wording “son of Rabbi Yose.” Guggenheimer’s translation follows the Rosh in reading “in the name of Rabbi Yose.” The Rashba’s quotation gives Rabbi Yisa, while Tosafot names R’ Yehudah. The heading’s kinship phrase remains open.
